And in the nineteenth year of Tiberius,
Abgar, king of Edessa, sent a painter,
whose name was John (Hannan?), the tabularius (archivist).
And he painted the likeness of our Lord Jesus on a board and brought it to Abgar.
He also sent a letter to our Lord by the hand of the same Hannan, saying:
"I have heard that miracles flow from You,
and that You grant healings without drugs.
Therefore, You are either God who came down from heaven,
or the Son of God.
And on this account, I have written requesting of You that You trouble Yourself and come to me,
and heal the disease which I have.
For I have also heard that the Jews are complaining {OCR?} against You,
and murmur against You,
and desire to do You harm.
Now I have a city, small and beautiful,
and it is sufficient for both of us."
Our Lord, however, replied to him:
"Blessed is the one who has believed in Me, while not having seen Me.
And concerning what you wrote, that I should come to you:
I have a mission (economy);
it is necessary that I fulfill here that for which I was sent,
and then I shall ascend to Him who sent Me.
And immediately I will send to you one of My disciples,
to heal your disease,
and give life to you and to those who are with you."
And in the very same nineteenth year of Tiberius, our Savior suffered, died, was buried, rose, and ascended into heaven.
And on the day of Pentecost, a great trembling seized the priests of the Jews,
for they heard a voice from within the Temple saying:
"Let us depart hence!"
And Abgar of Edessa wrote to Tiberius concerning all that the Jews had done to the Christ.
And he replied:
"Behold, on His account I have dismissed Pilate in disgrace,
and I shall take vengeance upon the Jews."
Now Herod the tetrarch,
he who was also named Antipas,
and was the son of Herod the slayer of the infants,
killed John,
and took Herodias, his brother's wife, while he was still alive.
And he was cast into exile along with Herodias,
and in Vienne (Viana? Vienna?) the city, he and she were killed.
